chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Anbasa ibn Bijad al-Abid, that a man said to al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both):
Advise me. So he said: Prepare your belongings and ready your supplies for a long journey. Be an advisor to yourself, and do not depend on anyone else to send you that which will rectify you.

key_terms.جهاز: Belongings, equipment for a journey -- metaphor for spiritual preparation for the afterlife
key_terms.زاد: Provisions, travel supplies -- metaphor for good deeds stored up for the Hereafter
key_terms.وصي: Guardian, advisor, executor of a will -- here meaning one who takes charge of their own spiritual affairs
key_terms.يصلحك: That which rectifies or benefits you -- referring to spiritual guidance and good works

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam al-Sadiq give about preparing for the afterlife?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked by a man for advice and responded with a profound metaphor comparing life to a journey toward the afterlife. He counseled the man to prepare spiritually for death and not to rely on others for his spiritual wellbeing, emphasizing personal responsibility in preparing good deeds as provisions for the Hereafter.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
